sentences.text: Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that the complainant has lodged complaint alleging that the appellant on threat committed sexual Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:25373 intercourse with her from 20.03.2023 to 25.12.2023.
It is also the case of the prosecution that the applicant has harassed the complainant, thus, forceful move has been done by the apellant, hence, FIR has been lodged against him.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.

He would further submit that the victim is aged about 21 years as such she is major lady, the appellant and the victim were known to each other, they were residing in rent in the same premises, thus, the act of the appellant was not forceful, it was an consensual relationship.

He would further submit that the offence has alleged to have been occurred from the period 20.03.2023 to 25.12.2023 and the FIR has been lodged on 13.03.2024, as such, there is delay in lodging the FIR and there is no explanation to the delay.

The appellant is in jail since 14.03.2024,
as such, he has already remained in jail for more than 4 months, the trial may take some time,
therefore, he may be released on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application and would submit that the appellant has committed forceful rape with the victim who is Scheduled Caste lady,
therefore, he may not be released on bail.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6. Considering the fact that the appellant has already remained in jail for more than 4 months,

considering the materials collected during investigation, also considering the medical evidence wherein no injury has been found in the private parts of the victim, the FIR has been lodged with delay of 3 months, therefore, I am inclined to release the appellant on bail.
7. Accordingly, the Criminal Appeal is allowed and the impugned order dated 13.05.2024 passed by the Special Judge in Bail Application Case No. 432/2024 is quashed.

It is directed that in the event of the appellant executing a personal bond for a sum of Rs. 25,000/- with a surety of Rs. 25,000/- to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, then he shall be released on bail.
He is directed to appear before Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:25373 the trial Court on each and every date given to him by the said Court till disposal of the trial.
8. The Trial Court is directed to conclude the trial within an outer limit of one year from today.
